reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern for this channel is a perfectly flat, zero-valued line under robust-standardized scaling. All four reference candidates exhibit no detectable variation: periodicity is absent (no oscillations), stability is maximal (zero roughness, curvature, and slope), baseline is exactly zero across all points, and there is no trend (linear, quadratic, or cubic coefficients are effectively zero in the standardized space). Amplitude is identically zero (90th-percentile amplitude = 0), peaks and troughs are undefined—there are no local extrema beyond the constant value. Noise is absent (MAD = 0, lower/upper extremes = 0). The only acceptable variation is numerical precision error near machine epsilon; any deviation above ~1e-4 in absolute value would be anomalous. This reflects a deterministic constant signal, likely representing a sensor idle state or a null channel. The consistency across 1P, 3P, and 5P windows confirms that the absence of dynamics is not an artifact of window length but an intrinsic property of the normal regime.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer the longest reliable reference (index 3, 5P) for queries with ≥5 cycles of data to maximize sensitivity to subtle deviations; for short queries (≤1 cycle), use index 0 (1P) as it matches query length exactly and avoids interpolation artifacts. All references are equally valid morphologically; selection should be based on query duration, not quality differences.
uncertainties: Whether true physical constancy or a preprocessing artifact (e.g., median/MAD standardization of a near-constant signal); however, consistency across independent intervals supports genuine normal behavior.
Exact tolerance for acceptable deviation (e.g., ±1e-4) must be calibrated per-channel during query analysis; no empirical noise floor is observable here.
